summary: Sustained 5xx for AtlasHealth AI in eu-west after parallel embedding uploads + long-lived streams — upstream fd leak causing runtime worker exits
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasHealth AI reported a sustained elevated 5xx rate starting ~2026-03-12 09:20 UTC from their production tenant in eu-west. The spike coincided with a scheduled data ingestion job that issued a high-concurrency embedding upload (multipart) while the product also maintained several long-lived chat streaming sessions.

Impact:
- Multiple customer endpoints returned 502/503 to end-users for ~2.5 hours with intermittent recoveries.
- Increased latency (p50 -> 600ms, p95 -> 3.6s) and ~18% request failure rate for the customer's tenant during the window.
- Business impact: degraded UX for AtlasHealth's clinical assistants; ticket raised by their on-call.

Environment:
- prod / eu-west (customer-dedicated capacity pool)
- Dedicated capacity (customer has reserved pool with 4 GPUs)
- Runtime version: serving-runtime v2.4.1
- Edge proxy: realtime-proxy v1.7.2

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Start large parallel embedding uploads from customer ingestion pipeline (50 concurrent multipart posts).
2) Maintain 15 active long-lived chat streaming sessions in parallel.
3) Observe elevated 5xx in API responses and runtime pool restarts within ~15-30 minutes.

Observed logs / telemetry snippets:
- api-gateway logs: repeated upstream 502 with "upstream reset: too many open files" and "connection reset by peer" messages.
- serving-runtime stderr (from one runtime instance): "ERROR: accept() failed: EMFILE (Too many open files)" followed by "worker process killed: exit_code=137" messages.
- node exporter fd count (runtime host): rose from ~1200 -> 32k during the ingestion window.
- edge-proxy traces show incremental backlog on accept queue and subsequent conn-close propagation.

Investigation notes (chronological):
- 09:25 UTC: Support alerted by AtlasHealth monitoring and support channel #support-enterprise.
- 09:28 UTC: Pager duty page to runtime on-call. Initial hypothesis: keepalive/connection leak or ephemeral port exhaustion in dedicated pool.
- 09:40 UTC: SRE observed rapidly increasing FD usage on 3/4 runtime hosts in the pool. Kernel shows many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT and some half-closed streams.
- 09:55 UTC: Reproduced at lower scale in staging by running customer ingestion + streaming client; confirmed steep FD growth in the realtime-proxy process tied to websocket connections that weren't being cleaned up after client disconnects.
- 10:30 UTC: Traced one failing code path in realtime-proxy: when upstream prefetch interplay occurs during multipart embed cancellation, an error path failed to close a wrapped websocket handle (third-party webhook integration code path).
- 11:05 UTC: Restarted offending runtime processes and realtime-proxy on the affected hosts as a mitigation. FD counts returned to baseline and 5xx rate dropped substantially.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Warm restart of runtime processes on affected hosts at 11:05 UTC (rebound seen ~11:10 UTC).
- Increased per-process soft ulimit for open files on dedicated-hosts to 65536 to give buffer while patch is prepared.
- Applied emergency rate limit for AtlasHealth tenant ingestion pipeline to throttle parallel multipart uploads (coordination with customer) to avoid immediate re-trigger.
- Added an on-call Grafana alert for rapid fd-growth (threshold: >5000 FDs or >200% baseline in 5m) for dedicated pools.

Root cause hypothesis and confirmation steps:
- Hypothesis: A rare error path in realtime-proxy (invoked by a combination of multipart embed cancellations + open streaming websocket sessions) did not close file descriptors / socket wrappers, causing fd leak and EMFILE on runtime, leading to worker exits and upstream 502/503.
- Confirmed by reproducing locally in staging and capturing process-level FD tables showing leaked websocket fds tied to a specific webhook/third-party integration code path.

Permanent remediation plan (engineering):
1) Patch realtime-proxy to ensure proper closure of websocket wrappers on all error/cancel paths and add unit tests for the multipart+stream cancellation scenario (PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-proxy/pull/1823).
2) Add FD-leak watchdog in serving-runtime to kill and auto-replace a worker that exceeds configurable FD growth thresholds (short-term guard).
3) Harden ulimits and systemd service configs in dedicated deploy artifacts to have safer defaults and alerting.
4) Update customer onboarding docs to recommend back-pressure configuration for heavy concurrent embedding uploads when long-lived streams are present.
5) Postmortem and runbook updates (Confluence) and a post-incident review with AtlasHealth CS.

Next steps / open follow-ups:
- PR 1823 needs code review and roll to canary; assigned to infra eng (Kenji).
- Create INT ticket to add automated FD growth detection in internal monitoring (linked INT-4092).
- Schedule a joint session with AtlasHealth engineering to review backlog/retry patterns and adjust client retry/backoff.
- After patch rollout, run targeted soak test using AtlasHealth reproduction case to validate fix and restore full ingestion concurrency.
